title: Work
description: Name the jobs, and say what you do.
grammar: ser and a profession, without an article
grammarNote: A profession goes straight after the verb: soy abogado, with no article in between.

explanation.summary: Every one of these jobs ends in -o and is masculine, and none of them takes an article. That is the rule: a profession is what you are, so it goes straight after the verb.

sections.heading: The jobs
sections.body: El abogado, el cocinero, el enfermero, el periodista, el policía, el programador, el diseñador, el veterinario, el taxista y el campesino are all masculine. Most of them end in -ero or -ista, and the ending makes the job: el programador programs, el taxista drives a taxi.

sections.heading: No article in between
sections.body: A profession goes straight after the verb, with no article: soy abogado, ella es enfermera. The feminine is easy: change the -o to -a, so el abogado becomes la abogada. When you use the job with an article, it is el abogado que trabaja aquí, the lawyer who works here.

items.note: Masculine: el abogado. The feminine is la abogada.
Masculine: el enfermero. The feminine is la enfermera.
Masculine: el policía. The feminine is la policía, with the same accent.
Masculine: el diseñador. The accent marks the stress.

drills.note: A profession takes no article after the verb.
The feminine of enfermero is enfermera.

drills.meaning: the teacher works at the school
drills.note: A profession with an article takes el or la.
No article between the verb and the job.
